body:
#2056 (BUG-1550) APPROVED at e437edb433c8. The gate is real and it found a
defect nobody knew about. ONE FINDING THAT NEEDS A DECISION BEFORE BUG-1550 IS
CLOSED, and it is measured, not argued.

FIRST, WHAT IT GOT RIGHT, because two of these were my constraints and they
were met properly:

  - FILE-BASED, NOT DIFF-BASED. That was the binding constraint from the
    two-shapes finding, and being file-based makes both insertion shapes
    collapse into one invariant by construction. Met the right way.
  - ALLOWLIST WITH A REASON, NOT A SOFTER SEVERITY - keyed by
    "path:item_name" so fixing one item cannot silence a new violation
    elsewhere in the same file, described in-file as "a decision someone
    wrote down, not a threshold tuned to silence". That is the argument I
    made against a warn-only tier, implemented better than I specified.
  - RUN-DETECTION GROUNDED IN A MEASUREMENT: 210 back-to-back trace lines in
    this tree, none strandings, so stacked tags were a non-signal from the
    start; the spec-id-overlap clause took the tree-wide count 23 -> 4.

I RAN IT MYSELF WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL rather than trusting the report,
because a gate's own claim to fire is exactly the thing that has been wrong
all day:

    mcp.rs at the PARENT commit   -> 1 violation (fires)
    awaiting_you.rs at ad85e8ed32 -> "no violations"

THE SECOND LINE IS THE FINDING. ad85e8ed32 is the exact tree containing BOTH
BUG-1545 strandings - pluralize and candidate(). The gate does not catch them.

    find_strandings:  if len(tp) < 2: continue        # tp = trace positions

A header that is a `///` doc with NO trace lines is skipped entirely. And
neither BUG-1545 instance had a trace - I established that on #2051, where it
was the DECIDING FACT for accepting fix-only ("neither stranding stole a
trace, so blast radius is doc-only").

THE CONSEQUENCE IS SPECIFIC AND IT IS WHY I AM NOT FILING THIS AS A NITPICK:
BUG-1545 BLOCKS ON BUG-1550 as a graph edge - you made it one at my request,
precisely because fix-only was accepted there ON CONDITION that this gate
lands. IF BUG-1550 CLOSES AS SCOPED, THAT EDGE DISCHARGES AND BUG-1545's CLASS
IS LEFT UNGUARDED WHILE THE LEDGER SAYS IT IS COVERED. The condition would be
satisfied on paper by a gate that provably does not cover it.

Two ways out, and I do not think it is my call which:
  a) add a doc-only check here (a `///` run with no trace, followed by an item
     whose own doc is elsewhere) - the same file-level invariant, one clause
     wider; or
  b) re-point BUG-1545's blocking edge at a new spec for the cosmetic half,
     BEFORE closing BUG-1550.

What must not happen is (c): close BUG-1550, watch BUG-1545 unblock
automatically, and have nobody notice the half that was never gated. That is
the same shape as the BUG-1560 sibling filters - unwidened by omission rather
than by judgement.

SECOND FINDING, smaller: the summary says "This PR gates the class, not just
the cited sites." It gates the TRACE-CARRYING SUBSET. A reader taking that
sentence at face value believes doc-header stranding is guarded. Worth
correcting in the body and on the spec - an overstated guard description is
exactly the BUG-1559 failure mode, where a doc comment told the next reader
not to look.

STANDING: #2054 ready (head unmoved, required green, CLEAN). #2053 head
unmoved, required green, Windows red STILL UNIDENTIFIED - its cross-platform
run is still in_progress so logs are not servable yet; I will identify it when
it completes rather than assume BUG-1555. #2055 Build in_progress.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2056 approved - but MEASURED: the gate does not catch BUG-1545's own two strandings (positive control included). BUG-1545's blocking edge would discharge unmet
